b: Guided off-road MTB in the Parco di Portofino and the Tigullio hills — panoramic climbs and forest/coast descents; a guide picks kid-safe lines.
g: Guided from your Chiavari base (operators meet in Chiavari/Sestri/Santa Margherita) — no car needed. Pre-confirm a 20"/24" kid MTB for Keir.

b: World MTB hub; a children's mountain-bike school on the Manie plateau (coached by a multi-time world champ) plus shuttle-served flow trails for the big brothers.
g: ~2h west by train (Finale Ligure Marina) + shuttle up to the plateau — a dedicated day. Schools supply age-right bikes.

n: Trail Arena Val Gardena — family flow trails
b: Your home valley's flow-trail bike park (graded 'Family Line' + freeride). CATCH: the bike gondola (Dantercepies) closes Oct 4 — shut before you arrive Oct 10, so no lift-served laps on your dates. Use Kronplatz for lifts; self-pedal/e-bike flow only here.
g: Drive (car leg) — but lift closed by your dates; see Kronplatz.

n: Alpe di Siusi & Seceda — gravel & trail by bike
b: Take bikes up the big cable cars onto the plateau for gentle high-meadow gravel and Seceda descents — the bike day that still works after the flow-trail lifts shut.
g: Drive to Ortisei/Siusi; the Alpe di Siusi & Seceda cable cars carry bikes and run to ~Nov 2.
k: Cable-car bike ticket ~€25-35pp; kid MTB rental ~€15-25

b: Rolling forest-and-vineyard off-road on gentle gravel/trail; book a private family operator (kid pedal MTBs for Keir, e-MTBs for the teens) — most stock e-bike tours are 14+/165cm and exclude a 9-yo.
g: Day-trip from Florence — operator collects you or starts near a train stop. Confirm a 24" kid MTB.

b: Ride the ancient basalt Appian Way and the Caffarella valley dirt trails through a huge archaeological park — off-tarmac gravel and cobbles, ruins along the way.
g: In Rome — bus to the park; EcoBike rents kids' bikes from age 4+ (120cm). Flat but genuinely off-road.

n: Colli Euganei — MTB in the volcanic hills
b: The real trail terrain near Venice: forest singletrack and gravel climbs over the Euganean Hills, with a marked MTB circuit — gentler perimeter gravel for Keir, hills for the teens.
g: Day-trip — ~40-min train Venice→Este/Monselice/Montegrotto, then local bike hire.

b: 18 lift-served mountain-bike trails off the Olang gondola, with skills parks to practise on before going up, plus rentals and a bike school. Crucially it runs to 8 Nov — nearly every other Alpine bike park has shut by then, so this is the ONE real park open on your dates.
g: Drive ~1h30 from Ortisei via the Puster valley — the one leg with the rental car. Grey's birthday is the 12th, so aim for Oct 11 or 13. Book kids' sizes ahead.
k: gondola + kid bike hire (call re: which of the 18 trails suit a 9-yo)

n: Pila Bike Park (Aosta) — kids' park, Sep 11–13 ONLY
b: The best kids' park found: green/blue family routes, a pump track, and FREE downhill courses for ages 6–12 at two bike schools. But 2026 lifts CLOSE Sun Sep 13 — a hard deadline.
g: Train Turin→Aosta ~2h, then a 5-min walk to the Aosta–Pila gondola — needs an Aosta overnight (sleep there Sep 11 or 12). Verify the Ivrea–Aosta line isn't on bus-replacement.
k: ~€146 lifts (kids €19) + kids' bikes/armor; the 9 & 12yo ride the free 6–12 course

n: Il Ciocco Bike Park (Barga) — family trails + pump track
b: Shuttle-served (no lift) but the best FAMILY bike experience on the route: Italy's largest indoor pump track, 70km incl. dedicated Easy & Family trails, qualified instructors, kids' rental.
g: Day-trip/overnight from Florence — train to Lucca then Barga-Gallicano (~40-50 min) + a short resort shuttle up the hill. Confirm Sept shuttle days + kid bike stock.
k: Pump track €20/€15; trail rental + lesson extra

n: Abetone Gravity Park — teens, September weekends only
b: A real gondola gravity park in the Tuscan Apennines, but September is WEEKENDS-ONLY (Sep 19/20/26) and it's DH/enduro — good for the 16/18-yo, not a 9-yo. Phone to confirm the late-Sept bike weekends actually run.
g: Florence→Pistoia→Abetone by bus, ~3h and sparse. Weekend of Sep 19-20 or 26 only.

b: A big family MTB complex — 25 trails, huge skills areas, pump tracks, beginner/family zones — and one of the very few alpine parks open to Nov 2. A backup to Kronplatz on the car leg.
g: Drive ~2h from Val Gardena (the car leg); carless-impossible otherwise.

n: Mottolino Bike Park (Livigno) — the full DH park (2-night trip)
b: The most American-style park: gondola, jumps, wooden features, downhill school, trails at every level — and open latest, to Sep 27. Serious DH suits the 12/16/18-yo; the 9-yo can do the lift-side blue with the school.
g: Bus Milano Centrale→Livigno ~4h30 — a 2-NIGHT trip out of Milan, not a day-trip.

n: La Mandria park — forest gravel spin
b: A 15km circular compact-gravel loop through oak forest with wildlife and picnic stops — safe, non-technical off-tarmac a 9-yo can do solo. Tamer than real trail riding.
g: ~12km from Turin centre by local transit/bike path.
